standard_prerequisites.name: Algebraic closure
standard_prerequisites.statement: The algebraic closure of A is the set of elements whose type over A is algebraic, and it is itself closed under the closure.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis A equals its algebraic closure.

standard_prerequisites.name: Unconfined system
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Steiner triple system admitting an HF-ordering without maximum.

standard_prerequisites.name: Neumann's lemma
standard_prerequisites.statement: Given elements outside the algebraic closure of A, any set in the monster model can be moved so that the chosen elements avoid it, over A.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the back-and-forth move used in the proof.

core_obligations: Expand the monster model by an HF-ordering, working inside the monster model (source line 791).
Apply Neumann's lemma to elements outside the algebraic closure of A in order to realise, over A, the types that the Tarski-Vaught criterion requires (source line 792).
Conclude that every formula with parameters in A and a witness in the ambient model has a witness in A, which is exactly elementarity (source line 792).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the expanded monster model and the ordering.
Use Neumann's lemma to realise the required types over A.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 789-790: if M is an unconfined Steiner triple system and A equals its algebraic closure inside M, then A is an elementary subsystem of M. The proof (source lines 791-793) is a compactness argument carried out in the monster model: the author expands the monster model by an HF-ordering, which is what makes the ambient structure unconfined, and then applies P. M. Neumann's lemma to move witnesses away from any prescribed set, which is precisely the step that turns a witness in the ambient model into a witness inside A for every formula with parameters in A. The statement records neither the expansion by the ordering nor the use of the permutation lemma.
